# Traceability (Doorstop)

Four [Doorstop](https://github.com/doorstop-dev/doorstop) documents form the chain:

| Prefix | Folder | Content | Parent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NEED` | `needs/` | stakeholder needs and project goals ("who needs what, and why") | - |
| `REQ` | `requirements/` | requirements: one testable "the software shall ..." statement each | NEED |
| `DES` | `design/` | design: how a requirement is implemented (files, functions, algorithms, decisions, limits) | REQ |
| `TST` | `tests/` | test specifications: which automated test proves the design, and the pass criterion | DES |

Rules (REQ002): every active normative REQ links to at least one NEED and
is implemented by a DES item; every DES is covered by at least one TST;
`doorstop` validation passes; `published/*.md` are up to date.
`tests/test_traceability.py` checks all of this.

The items shipped with the template (NEED001-002, REQ001-003, DES001-003,
TST001-003) describe the template's own machinery (LLM session archive,
this chain, the dev environment). Keep them - they are true of every
repository made from the template - and number your project's items after
them.

Commands (from the repository root, after `./setup.sh`; activate with
`source .venv/bin/activate` or prefix `.venv/bin/`):

```bash
doorstop                              # validate the whole tree
doorstop add REQ                      # create the next REQ item (edit the YAML file it prints)
doorstop link REQ004 NEED002          # link child -> parent
doorstop link DES004 REQ004
doorstop link TST004 DES004
doorstop review all                   # clear "unreviewed" after edits
doorstop clear all                    # clear "suspect link" after parent edits
tools/publish_traceability.sh         # regenerate published/{NEED,REQ,DES,TST}.md (committed)
doorstop publish all published/html   # browsable HTML with traceability matrix (gitignored)
```

Item files are YAML (`REQ001.yml` ...). `header` is the title, `text` the
normative statement, `links` the parent items, `level` the outline
position. Non-normative explanatory items can be added with
`normative: false`. Name the item in the code as well: a test's docstring
starts with its TST id, and a module or function implementing a DES item
mentions the DES id, so a reader can follow the chain in both directions.

DES001.yml
DES002.yml
DES003.yml

NEED002.yml

docs/traceability/published/:

REQ002.yml
REQ003.yml

docs/traceability/tests/:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerate the committed Markdown copies of the Doorstop documents
# (docs/traceability/published/*.md). tests/test_traceability.py fails when
# they are stale.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
DOORSTOP=.venv/bin/doorstop
"$DOORSTOP"
for doc in NEED REQ DES TST; do
    "$DOORSTOP" publish "$doc" "docs/traceability/published/$doc.md" >/dev/null
done
echo "published: docs/traceability/published/{NEED,REQ,DES,TST}.md"

"""TST002 - Doorstop traceability validation (REQ002, DES002): the chain NEED -> REQ -> DES -> TST is complete."""
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import yaml

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TRACE = ROOT / "docs" / "traceability"
DOCS = {"NEED": TRACE / "needs", "REQ": TRACE / "requirements", "DES": TRACE / "design", "TST": TRACE / "tests"}


def load(doc):
    items = {}
    for p in sorted(DOCS[doc].glob(f"{doc}*.yml")):
        items[p.stem] = yaml.safe_load(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return items


def links_of(item):
    out = []
    for link in item.get("links") or []:
        out.append(next(iter(link)) if isinstance(link, dict) else str(link))
    return out


def test_doorstop_validates():
    exe = ROOT / ".venv" / "bin" / "doorstop"

Four [Doorstop](https://github.com/doorstop-dev/doorstop) documents form the chain:

| Prefix | Folder | Content | Parent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NEED` | `needs/` | stakeholder needs and project goals ("who needs what, and why") | - |
| `REQ` | `requirements/` | requirements: one testable "the software shall ..." statement each | NEED |
| `DES` | `design/` | design: how a requirement is implemented (files, functions, algorithms, decisions, limits) | REQ |
| `TST` | `tests/` | test specifications: which automated test proves the design, and the pass criterion | DES |

Rules (REQ002): every active normative REQ links to at least one NEED and
is implemented by a DES item; every DES is covered by at least one TST;
`doorstop` validation passes; `published/*.md` are up to date.

this chain, the dev environment). Keep them - they are true of every

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
  One exception, legend kept: the tall segmented bar (*Figures* in `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`).
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""DES005 - the pivotal chart: Norwegian grade inflation versus IB Diploma stability,
with PISA (Norway, mathematics) as the external yardstick.

Reads only CSV files under sources/ and writes
  charts/grade_inflation_vs_ib.png / .svg           (three small multiples, raw units)
  charts/grade_inflation_vs_ib_indexed.png / .svg   (one panel, every series indexed to BASE_YEAR = 100)

Exits non-zero, naming the file or series, when a required input is missing.
Run from the repository root:  .venv/bin/python charts/make_chart.py [--base-year 2009]
"""
import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SRC = ROOT / "sources"
OUT = ROOT / "charts"

# dataviz skill reference palette (light surface): slot 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 aqua
COL_NO, COL_IB, COL_PISA, COL_REF = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#9a9892"
INK, INK2, SURFACE = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#fcfcfb"


def need(path: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if not path.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"make_chart: required input missing: {path.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    if df.empty:
        sys.exit(f"make_chart: required input is empty: {path.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return df


def series_or_exit(s: pd.Series, name: str) -> pd.Series:
    s = s.dropna()
    if len(s) < 2:
        sys.exit(f"make_chart: series '{name}' has fewer than two data points")
    return s.sort_index()


def load_series():
    # 1. Norway: grunnskolepoeng (national mean at end of lower secondary)
    gsp = need(SRC / "norway-grades" / "grunnskolepoeng.csv")
    gsp = gsp[gsp["value"].notna()].groupby("year")["value"].mean()
    norway = series_or_exit(gsp.astype(float), "grunnskolepoeng")

    # 2. IB Diploma: mean total points, May sessions
    ib = need(SRC / "ib-statistics" / "ib_session_stats.csv")
    ib = ib[(ib["month"].astype(int) == 5) & ib["mean_total_points"].notna()]
    ib_mean = series_or_exit(ib.set_index(ib["year"].astype(int))["mean_total_points"].astype(float), "IB mean total points")

    # 3. PISA mathematics, Norway and OECD average
    pisa = need(SRC / "pisa" / "pisa_country_year.csv")
    pisa = pisa[pisa["subject"].str.lower().eq("math") & pisa["mean"].notna()]
    def pick(name):
        sub = pisa[pisa["country"].str.lower().eq(name.lower())]
        return series_or_exit(sub.set_index(sub["year"].astype(int))["mean"].astype(float), f"PISA math {name}")
    pisa_no, pisa_oecd = pick("Norway"), pick("OECD average")
    return norway, ib_mean, pisa_no, pisa_oecd


def style(ax):
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    for side in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
    for side in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[side].set_color("#d9d8d4")
    ax.tick_params(colors=INK2, labelsize=9)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color="#e6e5e1", linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)


def endpoint_label(ax, s, color, fmt="{:.1f}"):
    for year in (s.index[0], s.index[-1]):
        ax.annotate(fmt.format(s[year]), (year, s[year]), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 7),
                    ha="center", fontsize=9, color=INK)


def small_multiples(norway, ib, pisa_no, pisa_oecd, xlim):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 4.6), facecolor=SURFACE)
    panels = [
        (axes[0], "Norwegian school grades rise", "Grunnskolepoeng, national mean (Udir)", norway, COL_NO, "{:.1f}"),
        (axes[1], "IB Diploma stays flat", "Mean total points, May session, worldwide (IB statistical bulletins)", ib, COL_IB, "{:.1f}"),
        (axes[2], "PISA falls", "PISA mathematics, mean score (OECD)", pisa_no, COL_PISA, "{:.0f}"),
    ]
    for ax, title, sub, s, col, fmt in panels:
        style(ax)
        ax.plot(s.index, s.values, color=col, linewidth=2, marker="o", markersize=4)
        endpoint_label(ax, s, col, fmt)
        ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=12, color=INK, fontweight="bold", pad=18)
        ax.text(0, 1.02, sub, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8.5, color=INK2)

Output in `/home/user/StoreClaudeWork/sources/ib-statistics/`:
- `ib_session_stats.csv` — 28 rows (May 2004–May 2026, Nov 2020–Nov 2024), 13 columns as specified; every cell traces to a snippet/file named in `source_url`/`note`; blanks where nothing was found.
- `ib_norway.csv` — no Norway-specific IB statistics exist in the bulletins (regional breakdown only); file records that plus two leads (Oslo International School page; Denmark's 2017 IB conversion table at uvm.dk and an IB email on worldwide means in a Folketing document).
- `REPORT.md` — series, regime changes, IB's own statements, caveats, full Sources table.
- `TO-FETCH.md` — ~35 bulletin PDF URLs (2007–2026, May and Nov, provisional/final) with the tables to extract; May 2006/2010/2017 URLs not captured (guesses flagged).

Constraints hit: ibo.org and all other non-GitHub hosts blocked (as expected); the shared WebSearch budget (200/turn) ran out after ~35 queries, so November 2005–2019 sessions, the 2017 pass rate, 2009 mean, and 2014/2015 45-point counts were not resolved. One GitHub-hosted transcription of the May/Nov 2024 bulletins (DevChrisChan/CiteCount, raw.githubusercontent.com) was downloaded and parsed; no mirrored bulletin PDFs found on GitHub.

### Mean total points (all diploma candidates) / pass rate / candidates with 45 points
- 2004 30.41 · 2005 30.09 / 81.4% · 2006 29.89 / 80.35% · 2007 29.56 / 78.78% · 2008 29.57 / 79.02% · 2009 — / 78.71%
- 2010 ~29.7 / 78.06% · 2011 ~29.7 / 77.75% ("no grade inflation" IB release) · 2012 29.85 / 78.48% · 2013 29.81 (29.96 final?) / 78.54% / 108
- 2014 ~30.1 / ~79.3% · 2015 29.88 / ~78.2% / 160 · 2016 30.07 / 79.28% / 146 · 2017 29.95 / — / 218 · 2018 29.78 (bulletin 29.76) / 78.18% / 259 · 2019 29.65 / 77.81% / 275 (166,465 candidates)
- 2020 (no exams) 31.34 final (29.92 provisional) / 85.18% / 339 (141 prov.) · 2021 (dual route) 33.02 / 88.96% / 1,351 (1,155 at results day) · 2022 (adapted boundaries) 32.00 / 86.11% / 772
- 2023 (return to pre-pandemic profile) 30.24 / 80.01% final (79.35% results day); 45-point count discontinued from this session · 2024 30.32 / 80.5% · 2025 30.58 / 81.3% · 2026 prov. 30.88 / 82.6% (third-party) ; 209,607 students; Middle East non-exam contingency
- Share of diploma candidates at 40–45 points (May 2024 bulletin charts): 2020 11.0%, 2021 18.4%, 2022 14.7%, 2023 8.9%, 2024 9.3%; 2025 final 11.9%. Share with 45 computed for 2020–22 only (0.38%, 1.53%, 0.87%).
- Mean of candidates *awarded* the diploma ≈ 2.5 pts higher: 32.15 (2012), 32.19 (2013), 32.23 (2019), 32.30 (2020), 33.15 (2021).
- Nov sessions 2020–24: 29.6, 32.3, 31.0, 29.1, 29.2 points; pass 75.8/87.2/82.0/72.4/72.7%.

Key IB statements captured: 2011 release (pass rates "not subject to the grade inflation trends seen with other educational systems"); May 2020 bulletin ("will not form part of the ongoing time series ... used to maintain standards"); July 2023 release ("profile of grade distribution returned close to pre-pandemic standards"); SRB research summary on boundary-setting.

Caveats flagged in REPORT: two populations (all candidates vs awarded), pass-rate definition break between old tabular bulletins (≤2019, ~78%) and Power BI bulletins (2020+, e.g. 2023 80.0 vs 79.35), provisional vs final figures, unlabeled chart readings for 2010/2011/2014/2015, cohort-mix growth in Asia, and the 2023→2026 upward drift of ~0.6 pts that the IB has not explained. Nothing was committed; raw downloads are in the scratchpad `ib-raw/` folder.

  Summary of findings
  
  1. IB design (documented from IB's own guides and research pages): DP assessment is "criterion-related, rather than measured against the performance of other exam takers"; exams are marked by external examiners who pass practice/qualification stages and are monitored during live on-screen marking by "seeds"; internal assessment is teacher-marked but externally moderated with group-level adjustments; coursework boundaries are fixed at course start. Grade boundaries are "agreed at a meeting of the senior examiners and IB staff ... using a combination of judgment, statistical evidence, grade descriptors and feedback from teachers"; the chief-examiner guide says "the grade standard from previous sessions must be carried forward". The statistical anchor is the "Statistically Recommended Boundaries" (SRB) method, which the IB itself calls "weak criterion referencing". An independent AlphaPlus review for the IB (lit review Dec 2021, simulation Sept 2022, exec summary Oct 2022) found the method "superior to many other approaches as it aims to account for any change in cohort ability, though weaker than using prior attainment", with assumptions met in "only around half of IB's contexts". IRT/Rasch appears only in research (Badham, Meadows & Baird 2025, Frontiers), not operational awarding. Pandemic: calculated grades May 2020 (then adjusted after ~700/3,020 schools complained), per-route boundaries Nov 2020, mean rose 31.34 (M20) to 33.02 (M21), and the IB explicitly "set the distribution of awarded grades to the pre-pandemic levels of May 2019" in May 2023 (mean 30.24; M25 mean 30.6, pass 81.9%). External/internal share only from third-party sources (typically 20-25% IA, 70-80% external; higher IA in arts) — subject guides needed. Structural facts (6 subjects x 1-7, 3 core points, 45 max, 24 min, failing conditions) are labelled UNVERIFIED (model memory) except the 24/45 figures.
  
  2. ACER/ISA answer: the user's belief is NOT supported. ACER's ISA is a PISA-framework test for grades 3-10 used by international schools of many curricula. The IB's documented relationship with ACER is as a research client: IB contracted ACER in 2009 to analyse ISA data for PYP/MYP schools (reports 2010, 2021, 2026), ACER did the 2012 Australian university-outcomes study and a 2019 digital-assessment report for the IB. DP assessment is designed and run by the IB's own Assessment Centre in Cardiff (200+ staff, "responsible for creating and managing assessment activities for the IB's four programmes") with an "Assessment Research and Design" team inside the Assessment Principles and Practice unit; the external methodological reviewers the IB cites are AlphaPlus, Ecctis/UK NARIC and Oxford researchers, not ACER. PISA: ACER led the consortium for PISA 2000-2012 (sources differ on whether the lead ended 2012 or 2015); ETS managed PISA 2018 and was Core A contractor for 2022; ACER returned as Core 1 contractor for PISA 2025. "ETS from 2015" is unverified by search.
  
  3. Key studies: HESA for IB 2011/2016/2021 (Duxbury et al. 2021: IB holders 3.02x more likely to get a first, 40% more likely 2:1+, after controlling for ability) — all IB-commissioned; Green & Vignoles 2012 (Cambridge Assessment, independent) found the UCAS tariff OVERvalued the IB — must be acknowledged; Edwards & Underwood (ACER) 2012 Australia: parity after controls but higher correlation of secondary grades with university performance for IB graduates; Caspary & Bland 2011 Florida and Shah/Dean/Chen 2010 UC: IB exam score strongest predictor of college GPA. UK NARIC 2019 Norway alignment study (DP compatible with Norwegian system) is a curriculum alignment study, not performance. Precedents: Australia replaced the "too generous" whole-score ATAR conversion (45 -> 99.95) with a fine-grained conversion using subject percentage marks (results 2023/admission 2024; 60% unchanged, 25% up, 15% down) — i.e. more resolution, not compression; Sweden cut max meritvarde to 44-45 in 2016, IB applications fell, UHR's 2022 impact assessment conceded "felaktig meritvardering"; Denmark has an ongoing under-valuation debate (IB 6 = 10.8). Norway: HK-dir table Dec 2022; hearings 2024, winter 2025 and autumn 2026 (deadline 10.12.2026, effective 2030-31); the only quantitative justification found is "0.08% of Norwegian applicants vs 2.8% of IB applicants at 6.0"; method is HK-dir's Norsk Regnesentral-reviewed statistical mapping; HK-dir (global data) and the Ministry (Norway-only data, start at 20 points) disagree on the reference population. Norwegian grading: standpunkt set by teacher's "faglige skjonn" against kompetansemal (forskrift kap. 3, Udir-2-2020), exam draw under Udir-2-2018/§ 9-30; all exams cancelled 2020 and 2022, written exams 2021; Udir says 2019-20 to 2021-22 averages are not comparable; Lillebo, Skalholt & Kindt (TfS 2024) report rising averages and easier completion; a KD-commissioned project on grade inflation/segregation is under way (2026).
  
  4. Gaps: no Norwegian study of IB graduates' university performance (medicine or otherwise) was found — the authorities' argument is purely distributional; no UK NARIC 2016 IB/A-level benchmark found; IA/external weightings need subject guides; Udir grade-trend series, exact Vg3 exam count, HK-dir method note and the actual 2022/2025/2026 tables still to fetch (all listed in TO-FETCH.md). Caveat for the op-ed: nearly all predictive-validity evidence is IB-commissioned, the IB's model is self-described "weak criterion referencing" with statistically managed distributions, and the IB visibly inflated grades in 2020-22 before correcting.

entries.description: Get a specific label from a repository.

entries.name: mcp__github__issue_write
entries.description: Create a new or update an existing issue in a GitHub repository.

assignees.description: Usernames to assign to this issue

duplicate_of.description: Issue number that this issue is a duplicate of. Required when state_reason is 'duplicate'.

delete.description: Set to true to clear this field's current value on the issue. When false or omitted, this property is ignored. Cannot be true when 'value' or 'field_option_name' is provided.

field_name.description: Issue field name (case-insensitive). Must match a field returned by list_issue_fields for this repository or its organization.

field_option_name.description: Option name for single-select fields. Validated against the field's options before the API call. Cannot be combined with 'value' or 'delete: true'.

value.description: Value to set. Use for text, number, and date fields (date as YYYY-MM-DD). For single-select fields, prefer 'field_option_name' so the option is validated before the API call. Cannot be combined with 'field_option_name' or 'delete: true'.

issue_fields.description: Issue field values to set or clear. Each item requires 'field_name' and exactly one of 'value', 'field_option_name', or 'delete: true'.

labels.description: Labels to apply to this issue

method.description:
Write operation to perform on a single issue.
Options are:
- 'create' - creates a new issue.
- 'update' - updates an existing issue.

parent_issue_number.description: Issue number of the parent issue. Only used when method is 'create' and cannot be combined with issue_fields. The new issue is created and attached to this parent in the same operation.

parent_owner.description: Repository owner of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_repo. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.

parent_repo.description: Repository name of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_owner. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.

state_reason.description: Reason for the state change. Ignored unless state is changed.

type.description: Type of this issue. For updates, pass null to remove the current type. Only use if issue types are enabled for this repository. Use list_issue_types to get valid type values for this repository or its owner organization. If the repository doesn't support issue types, omit this parameter.

entries.name: mcp__github__list_issues
entries.description: List issues in a GitHub repository. For pagination, use the 'endCursor' from the previous response's 'pageInfo' in the 'after' parameter.

after.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the cursor from the previous response.

direction.description: Order direction. If provided, the 'orderBy' also needs to be provided.

field_name.description: Name of the custom field (e.g. "Priority"). Case-insensitive.

# Synthesis: what the evidence base says (first pass, 2 Nov 2026)

This note pulls the key findings of the seven evidence folders together for the
op-ed. Every number below is traced in the folder named in brackets; most come
from search-engine snippets of primary documents, because the cloud session
could not open the source websites. **Verify against the primary documents in
each folder's `TO-FETCH.md` before quoting verbatim.**

## 1. The case in one chart

`charts/grade_inflation_vs_ib.png` (small multiples, same relative y-scale)
and `charts/grade_inflation_vs_ib_indexed.png` (one panel, 2012 = 100):

| Yardstick | Start | End | Change | Folder |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Norwegian grunnskolepoeng, national mean | 39.5 (2009) | 42.2 (2026); peak 43.4 (2022, no exams) | +2.7 points (+7 %) | norway-grades |
| IB Diploma mean total points, May, worldwide | 30.4 (2004); 29.65 (2019) | 30.9 (2026, provisional); 30.24 (2023) | about +0.5 since 2004, +0.6 since the 2023 reset | ib-statistics |
| PISA mathematics, Norway | 495 (2003); 502 (2015 peak) | 452 (2025) | -50 since 2015, about 2.5 school years by the OECD's 20-points rule | pisa |

The pandemic band is the natural experiment: when ordinary exams disappeared,
*both* systems inflated (grunnskolepoeng +1.2 in one year; IB mean 29.65 to
33.02). The IB then deliberately "set the distribution of awarded grades to
the pre-pandemic levels of May 2019" in 2023 (mean back to 30.24). Norwegian
grades came only part of the way down and have settled about 2.7 points above
2009. An externally anchored system corrects; a teacher-set system ratchets.

## 2. Norwegian grade inflation is documented by the authorities themselves

- Udir on upper secondary: "I løpet av de siste 15 årene har elevene i de
  fleste fellesfagene i videregående opplæring fått stadig bedre karakterer.
  Undersøkelser viser imidlertid ikke den samme utviklingen i elevenes
  kompetanse" (norway-grades).
- Nearly half of upper-secondary pupils get a lower grade on the written exam
  than their standpunkt grade; 41 % in lower secondary (Udir, SSB).
- National tests (nasjonale prøver): no change in mean scale points 2014-2021
  while grunnskolepoeng rose; declines in 2023 and 2024 (norway-grades).
- The ministry itself commissioned research in 2026 on "kvalitet,
  karakterinflasjon og segregering" in upper secondary (norway-grades).
- Upper-secondary maths programme subjects (R1, R2, S1, S2) show the same
  ratchet: R1 standpunkt 3.9 (2007-2015) to 4.2 (2017-2021) to 4.0 (2023-2026)
  (norway-grades, `vgs_grades.csv`).
- PISA: Norway's maths decline 2018-2025 (-49) is the largest among the 16
  comparison countries; 38 % of 15-year-olds are now below Level 2 in maths,
  against 17-22 % in every cycle 2003-2018 (pisa).

## 3. The IB is built to hold its standard; Norwegian standpunkt grades are not

- IB: externally marked exams, moderated internal assessment, grade boundaries
  set at a grade-award meeting from judgement plus statistics, with the chief
  examiner guide stating "the grade standard from previous sessions must be
  carried forward". The statistical anchor (Statistically Recommended
  Boundaries) was reviewed independently by AlphaPlus in 2021-2022
  (ib-assessment-design).
- Norwegian standpunkt grades are set by the teacher's "faglige skjønn" against
  kompetansemål with no external anchoring; only a few exams are drawn by lot;
  all exams were cancelled in 2020 and 2022 (ib-assessment-design, norway-grades).
- Honest caveats to keep in the op-ed: the IB calls its own model "weak
  criterion referencing"; it visibly inflated in 2020-2022 before correcting;
  the mean has drifted up about 0.6 points since 2023 without an IB
  explanation; nearly all predictive-validity studies are IB-commissioned, and
  an independent Cambridge Assessment study (Green and Vignoles 2012) found the
  UK tariff *over*-valued the IB (ib-assessment-design).
- The ACER / ISA belief is not supported: ACER has only been a research
  contractor to the IB; DP assessment is designed and run by the IB's own
  Assessment Centre in Cardiff. ACER did lead the PISA consortium 2000-2012 and
  is back as a PISA 2025 contractor (ib-assessment-design).

## 4. The conversion table: what changed and what the method assumes

| IB points | Table in force (1999 regulation) | 2022 HK-dir table | 2026 proposal |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | 26.0 | 20.0 | 29.5 |
| 24 | 34.3 | 29.0 | ? |
| 30 | 42.9 | 40.4 | ? |
| 35 | 50.0 | 47.4 | ? |
| 40 | 57.1 | 53.6 | ? |
| 42-45 | 60.0 (plateau from 42) | 45 only = 60.0 | ? (Legeforeningen's annex: 45 = 60.0) |

(conversion-table, `tables_norway.csv`; rows 22-45 of the 2026 proposal were
not visible in any snippet and are the top fetch priority.)

- Method: the admission regulation says tables "skal lagast ved å finne
  prosentilar i det utanlandske datagrunnlaget"; HK-dir / Norsk Regnesentral
  match the empirical cumulative distribution (ecdf) of IB totals to the
  distribution of Norwegian vitnemål averages. The minister called it "en ren
  statistisk sammenligning av populasjonene" (conversion-table).
- The only quantitative justification found: "0,08 % av søkerne med norsk
  videregående opplæring (studieforberedende) fikk snitt 6,0 i opptaket, mens
  2,8 % av IB-søkerne fikk dette" (press release 29 Oct 2026). The method
  therefore assumes IB and Norwegian applicants have the same ability
  distribution and treats the Norwegian distribution, inflation included, as
  the reference. Nobody has published Norwegian outcome data on how IB
  graduates actually perform at university (media-and-policy,
  ib-assessment-design).
- Medicine, UiO autumn, ordinary quota: cut-off 68.0 (2011) to 70.2 (2023) to
  69.0 (2026); first-time-diploma quota 61.6 (2020) to 60.0 (2026). A 45-point
  diploma converts to 60.0 under every table, so the fight is over 38-44 points
  (media-and-policy, norway-grades).
- Timeline: old table since the 1990s; HK-dir table 15 Dec 2022 for the
  2025/26 intake; NIBS letter May 2023; Storting questions autumn 2024 and
  Dok 8:76 S (Feb 2025, H, FrP, SV, V, KrF); minister Aasland postponed and
  re-heard in winter 2025; new hearing 29 Oct 2026 (deadline 10 Dec 2026,
  effective from the 2030-31 intake, built only on Norwegian IB-line data)
  (media-and-policy, `timeline.csv`).

## 5. The Western record: teacher grades rise, external measures do not

- UK A-level A*/A share: 25.4 % (2019), 38.1 % (2020, teacher grades),
  44.8 % (2021), back to 27.2 % (2023) under Ofqual's "comparable outcomes".
  Regulators anchor school grades to external evidence, never the reverse.
- US: mean high-school GPA 2.68 (1990) to 3.11 (2019) while SAT and NAEP fell.
- Germany: share of 1.0-1.9 Abitur 20.1 % (2006) to 30.7 % (2024).
- Denmark: STX average 6.9 (2010) to 7.7 (2022); exam grades 0.8 below teacher
  year grades. Sweden: decades of betygsinflation research and a 2023 inquiry
  "för att stoppa betygsinflationen".
- Every earlier IB-conversion dispute (UK tariff, Australia ATAR 2021-2023,
  Sweden 2016, Denmark 2018) was about top-end resolution and the choice of
  comparison group, the same two design questions as Norway's
  (grade-inflation-international).

## 6. Gaps to close before publication

1. Full 2026 proposal table (rows 22-45) and the HK-dir "2026a/2026b" variants.
2. Per-subject upper-secondary standpunkt and exam series (one Udir API fetch).
3. Norwegian applicants' grade-average distribution over time (DBH / HK-dir).
4. IB bulletins: 2009 mean, 2017 pass rate, 45-point counts 2014-2015, Norway
   has no country breakdown (regional only).
5. Foreign conversion tables beyond Denmark; Storting committee outcome on
   Dok 8:76 S; any VG, BT, Aftenposten, NRK coverage (none surfaced in search).
EOF

+# Synthesis: what the evidence base says (first pass, 2 Nov 2026)
+This note pulls the key findings of the seven evidence folders together for the
+op-ed. Every number below is traced in the folder named in brackets; most come
+from search-engine snippets of primary documents, because the cloud session
+could not open the source websites. **Verify against the primary documents in
+| Norwegian grunnskolepoeng, national mean | 39.5 (2009) | 42.2 (2026); peak 43.4 (2022, no exams) | +2.7 points (+7 %) | norway-grades |
+| IB Diploma mean total points, May, worldwide | 30.4 (2004); 29.65 (2019) | 30.9 (2026, provisional); 30.24 (2023) | about +0.5 since 2004, +0.6 since the 2023 reset | ib-statistics |
+| PISA mathematics, Norway | 495 (2003); 502 (2015 peak) | 452 (2025) | -50 since 2015, about 2.5 school years by the OECD's 20-points rule | pisa |
+The pandemic band is the natural experiment: when ordinary exams disappeared,
+*both* systems inflated (grunnskolepoeng +1.2 in one year; IB mean 29.65 to
+33.02). The IB then deliberately "set the distribution of awarded grades to
+the pre-pandemic levels of May 2019" in 2023 (mean back to 30.24). Norwegian
+grades came only part of the way down and have settled about 2.7 points above
+2009. An externally anchored system corrects; a teacher-set system ratchets.
+## 2. Norwegian grade inflation is documented by the authorities themselves
+- Udir on upper secondary: "I løpet av de siste 15 årene har elevene i de
+  fleste fellesfagene i videregående opplæring fått stadig bedre karakterer.
+  Undersøkelser viser imidlertid ikke den samme utviklingen i elevenes
+- Nearly half of upper-secondary pupils get a lower grade on the written exam
+  than their standpunkt grade; 41 % in lower secondary (Udir, SSB).
+- National tests (nasjonale prøver): no change in mean scale points 2014-2021
+  while grunnskolepoeng rose; declines in 2023 and 2024 (norway-grades).
+- The ministry itself commissioned research in 2026 on "kvalitet,
+  karakterinflasjon og segregering" in upper secondary (norway-grades).
+- Upper-secondary maths programme subjects (R1, R2, S1, S2) show the same
+- PISA: Norway's maths decline 2018-2025 (-49) is the largest among the 16
+  comparison countries; 38 % of 15-year-olds are now below Level 2 in maths,
+## 3. The IB is built to hold its standard; Norwegian standpunkt grades are not
+- IB: externally marked exams, moderated internal assessment, grade boundaries
+  set at a grade-award meeting from judgement plus statistics, with the chief
+  examiner guide stating "the grade standard from previous sessions must be
+  carried forward". The statistical anchor (Statistically Recommended
+  Boundaries) was reviewed independently by AlphaPlus in 2021-2022
+- Norwegian standpunkt grades are set by the teacher's "faglige skjønn" against
+  kompetansemål with no external anchoring; only a few exams are drawn by lot;
+  all exams were cancelled in 2020 and 2022 (ib-assessment-design, norway-grades).
+- Honest caveats to keep in the op-ed: the IB calls its own model "weak
+  criterion referencing"; it visibly inflated in 2020-2022 before correcting;
+  the mean has drifted up about 0.6 points since 2023 without an IB
+  explanation; nearly all predictive-validity studies are IB-commissioned, and
+  an independent Cambridge Assessment study (Green and Vignoles 2012) found the
+- The ACER / ISA belief is not supported: ACER has only been a research
+  contractor to the IB; DP assessment is designed and run by the IB's own
+  Assessment Centre in Cardiff. ACER did lead the PISA consortium 2000-2012 and
+  is back as a PISA 2025 contractor (ib-assessment-design).
+## 4. The conversion table: what changed and what the method assumes
+| IB points | Table in force (1999 regulation) | 2022 HK-dir table | 2026 proposal |
+not visible in any snippet and are the top fetch priority.)
+- Method: the admission regulation says tables "skal lagast ved å finne
+  prosentilar i det utanlandske datagrunnlaget"; HK-dir / Norsk Regnesentral
+  match the empirical cumulative distribution (ecdf) of IB totals to the
+  distribution of Norwegian vitnemål averages. The minister called it "en ren
+- The only quantitative justification found: "0,08 % av søkerne med norsk
+  videregående opplæring (studieforberedende) fikk snitt 6,0 i opptaket, mens
+  2,8 % av IB-søkerne fikk dette" (press release 29 Oct 2026). The method
+  therefore assumes IB and Norwegian applicants have the same ability
+  distribution and treats the Norwegian distribution, inflation included, as
+  the reference. Nobody has published Norwegian outcome data on how IB
+- Medicine, UiO autumn, ordinary quota: cut-off 68.0 (2011) to 70.2 (2023) to
+  diploma converts to 60.0 under every table, so the fight is over 38-44 points
+- Timeline: old table since the 1990s; HK-dir table 15 Dec 2022 for the
+  2025/26 intake; NIBS letter May 2023; Storting questions autumn 2024 and
+  Dok 8:76 S (Feb 2025, H, FrP, SV, V, KrF); minister Aasland postponed and
+  re-heard in winter 2025; new hearing 29 Oct 2026 (deadline 10 Dec 2026,
+  effective from the 2030-31 intake, built only on Norwegian IB-line data)
+## 5. The Western record: teacher grades rise, external measures do not
+- UK A-level A*/A share: 25.4 % (2019), 38.1 % (2020, teacher grades),
+  Regulators anchor school grades to external evidence, never the reverse.
+- US: mean high-school GPA 2.68 (1990) to 3.11 (2019) while SAT and NAEP fell.
+- Denmark: STX average 6.9 (2010) to 7.7 (2022); exam grades 0.8 below teacher
+  year grades. Sweden: decades of betygsinflation research and a 2023 inquiry
+- Every earlier IB-conversion dispute (UK tariff, Australia ATAR 2021-2023,
+  Sweden 2016, Denmark 2018) was about top-end resolution and the choice of
+  comparison group, the same two design questions as Norway's
+1. Full 2026 proposal table (rows 22-45) and the HK-dir "2026a/2026b" variants.
